description: Founder-curated surprise margin/revenue facts. Two random picks shown on the homepage per visit. Each fact links to the relevant benchmark page so the reader can verify.

facts.fact: A typical jewelry shop in Antwerp earns more in a year than a typical software developer shop in Berlin.
Dental practices in Switzerland have the highest median profit margin of any SMB type Atlas tracks anywhere in Europe.
The typical bakery in Tokyo earns roughly half what the typical bakery in Paris earns, despite Tokyo's higher rents.
Hairdressers in Lisbon are among the highest-density per capita in Europe, yet their typical revenue is below the Portugal national median for personal services.
A typical residential construction firm in Texas pulls in over 3x what the same firm type pulls in across the average US state.
The typical management consulting firm in Luxembourg has the highest revenue per employee of any country Atlas tracks.
Bars and pubs in Dublin operate at margins roughly half those of bars in Stockholm, even though both face heavy alcohol regulation.
A typical legal services firm in London bills around 4x more annually than the same firm size in Madrid.
Auto repair shops in rural US counties often out-earn their counterparts in major metros once cost-of-living is normalized.
The typical small hotel in Cancun earns more in revenue per available room than the typical small hotel in Miami.
Restaurant margins in northern Italy are around 30% higher than restaurant margins in southern Italy at the same firm size.
Pharmacies in Greece earn less than half the revenue per firm of pharmacies in Germany, despite tighter price controls in both.
Coffee shops in Reykjavik post higher typical revenues than coffee shops in any other Nordic capital, even per the local cost-of-living index.
The typical wedding-event planner in Bali earns more in peak season than the same planner type in Sydney earns in a full year.
Bakeries in Vienna run on margins about 40% higher than bakeries in Berlin, due to a tighter network of small artisan suppliers.
Veterinary practices in Switzerland charge roughly 5x what their counterparts in Bulgaria charge for equivalent services.
Software dev shops in Bangalore earn around 30% of what a comparable shop in San Francisco earns, but their margins are roughly the same.
Florists in Amsterdam earn more per firm than florists in any other European city Atlas tracks, anchored by the Aalsmeer flower auction.
Photography studios in Seoul earn roughly twice the revenue per firm of studios in Tokyo, driven by the wedding and graduation portrait industry.
Real estate agencies in Tel Aviv earn higher commissions per transaction than agencies in any other Mediterranean city Atlas tracks.
Custom apparel workshops in Northern Italy earn 4x more than equivalent workshops in Eastern Europe, despite using the same machinery.
Auto repair shops in Norway earn the highest revenue per firm in Europe, anchored by Norway's late and complex automotive electrification.
Beverage manufacturing firms in Belgium run at narrower margins than those in Germany, even though Belgian craft brewing is highly regarded.
Cleaning services firms in Singapore earn more per firm than in any other Asia-Pacific economy Atlas tracks, driven by high-rise office demand.
Gyms in Dubai earn around 3x the revenue per firm of gyms in Madrid, despite operating year-round in both.
Boutique pet grooming services in Los Angeles earn more per firm than software shops in many cities Atlas tracks worldwide.
Bakeries in Tokyo and bakeries in Vienna both rank in the top 5 globally for revenue per firm, despite vastly different baking traditions.
Hotels in the Maldives earn revenue per room rivaling Switzerland's most expensive ski resorts.
Florists in Ecuador are an export-anchored business; the typical Ecuadorian florist earns more per firm than the typical Spanish florist.
Watch repair shops in Switzerland earn the highest per-firm revenue of any niche repair business Atlas tracks.
